name: folders
intent: The user-data folders every machine shares with vg-dotfiles-windows, in the home directory (~/vg-workspace with projects, school and work; ~/vg-studio; ~/vg-documents; ~/vg-library; ~/vg-tools), and the machine repos (vg-paradigms, vg-deployments, vg-wallpapers) cloned beside the vg-dotfiles checkout.

text: The ~/vg-* tree mirrors vg-dotfiles-windows' C:\vg-* folders, in the home directory on every Nix archetype
why: The user wants one layout across Windows, NixOS, NixOS-WSL and macOS, kept in the home folder here rather than at the root. The list matches home.psd1's `folders` (vg-dotfiles-windows), relative to the home directory, created by a home-manager activation step (mkdir -p: idempotent, and the same on macOS, where tmpfiles doesn't exist). Applied on vgwsl2: all 13 folders created.

text: The machine repos are cloned beside the checkout, clone-only, and a clone that can't happen warns
why: vg-dotfiles-windows' graft 01a165b4 asks every host to clone vg-paradigms, vg-deployments and vg-wallpapers beside the dotfiles checkout, as Windows does; project repos are deliberately not cloned. All three are private: HTTPS through gh's git credential helper (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0), then SSH with the host's key (BatchMode, accept-new for GitHub's host key), so activation never prompts. An existing clone is never pulled or reset. Checked on vgwsl2 with neither gh login nor key: each repo warns and the rebuild completes. A successful clone isn't tested yet. The slideshow over vg-wallpapers (the rest of that graft) isn't done.

text: vgwsl2 runs NixOS VM tests on KVM once Windows exposes AMD-V
why: Other projects' `nix flake check` (Jacquard's VM tests) should run locally. The user is in the kvm group; Nix's system-features already include kvm and nixos-test (the NixOS default). WSL ships kvm-amd as a module (CONFIG_KVM_AMD=m, in /lib/modules), but after a WSL restart with nestedVirtualization=true the guest still had no svm flag and `Hyper-V: Nested features: 0x0` (VBS running), so the Windows side is asked by graft 01a165ae-63a0-71f3-9676-bf2acd806114 (vg-dotfiles-windows).

title: vgwsl2: check /dev/kvm once Windows exposes AMD-V; load kvm-amd only if it's still missing
body: After the Windows fix and a WSL restart: grep -c svm /proc/cpuinfo > 0; ls -l /dev/kvm (group kvm, 0660); if missing, try `modprobe kvm_amd` first, then declare boot.kernelModules = [ "kvm-amd" ] only if that's what makes it appear (WSL uses Microsoft's kernel). Then run a NixOS VM test to confirm.
